sources.entry: Vanilla Cookbook - Recipe manager designed with complexity under the hood, keeping the user experience as uncluttered, simply vanilla as possible. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Vanilla Cookbook is a self-hosted recipe manager that parses messy recipe text into clean ingredient lists with minimal setup and an uncluttered interface.
summary.what_it_does: It parses free-text ingredient strings into quantity, unit and ingredient parts, and supports scaling recipes while keeping the original text format. It converts US volumetric measures to metric or imperial weights and translates inline temperatures, fractions and ranges. Recipes can be imported via a browser bookmarklet or by pasting a URL, with scraping of hundreds of sites claimed, and exported. It also includes a shopping list, cooking logs with a calendar view, user management with optional OAuth/OpenID Connect login, and public recipe sharing with forking and favouriting. Optional LLM features (Google, OpenAI, Anthropic or Ollama API keys) add HTML parsing fallback, recipe tweaking, translation, prompt-based recipe generation, image analysis and semantic search.
use_cases: planning a shopping list from recipes
how_to_run: Download the .env and docker-compose.yml template files from the repo root (curl commands given in README)
Set ORIGIN in .env to the URL the app will be hosted on
On first run, enter admin user details
Local dev: git clone --recursive, cp .env.template .env, pnpm i, pnpm dev:setup, pnpm dev
notable: Ingredient parsing is text-string based, so users get scaled, structured ingredients without manual data entry
Single Docker container with a portable SQLite database
Automated scheduled and pre-migration SQLite backups
Optional LLM assist features with support for several providers including Ollama for local models
Progressive Web App with share-to-scrape from mobile browsers
caveats: Several features (LLM assist, OAuth) need extra API keys or identity-provider setup
Reverse proxies such as nginx may need body size and proxy buffer changes to save recipes with images
Local dev requires native build tools for better-sqlite3
Upgrading from older images that wrote root-owned files requires a manual ownership migration
